title: Implantable loop recorder
what: A small device about the size of a USB stick is placed under the skin of your chest. It records your heart rhythm for years.
why: For rare fainting spells or skipped beats that cannot be caught on a regular ECG or a 24-hour monitor.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; the device usually works for up to several years
tell_doctor: How often your episodes happen and what they are like

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast is usually fine. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. The doctor will tell you what to take on the day.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes that do not press on your chest.

steps: You lie on the table, and your chest is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing injection is given under the skin on the left side of your chest
The doctor makes a small cut
The device is slipped under the skin
The cut is closed with a stitch or skin glue
The device is set up, and you are shown how to use it
feel: The numbing injection lasts a few seconds
During the procedure, you feel pressure but no pain
The spot may ache for a couple of days
after: Keep the area dry until your doctor allows
During an episode, press the button on the handheld device, if you have one
Data is sent to your doctor. The clinic will tell you how often
When you no longer need the device, it is removed just as simply
red_flags: Redness, swelling, or pus where the device was placed
Fainting or severe chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have an MRI with it?
faq.a: Most of these devices are MRI-safe under certain conditions. Show your device card before the scan.

faq.q: Does the device treat the rhythm?
faq.a: No. It only records. Based on the recording, the doctor decides what treatment you need.

reminders.text: Heart monitor placement tomorrow. Bring documents, past ECGs, and your list of medicines.
